source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

title: What if athletes were allowed to take drugs?

lines.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.
lines.zh: 哈囉，這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。我是 Neil。

lines.en: And I'm Pippa.
lines.zh: 我是 Pippa。

lines.en: Sharing your Netflix password, lying about your age or not paying the bus fare are a few examples of cheating in daily life.
lines.zh: 分享 Netflix 密碼、謊報年齡、不付公車錢，都是日常生活中作弊的例子。

lines.en: But there's one place where cheating is usually considered wrong, and that's sport.
lines.zh: 但有一個地方，作弊通常被認為是錯的，那就是運動。

lines.en: Cheating in sport through the use of performance-enhancing drugs, informally called doping, is normally considered wrong.
lines.zh: 在運動中使用提升表現的藥物來作弊，非正式的說法叫 doping（用禁藥），通常被認為是錯的。

lines.en: Just ask American cycling legend Lance Armstrong, who was thrown out of the sport for using banned substances.
lines.zh: 問問美國自行車傳奇人物 Lance Armstrong 就知道了，他因為使用禁用物質而被逐出這項運動。

lines.en: But earlier this year, a sporting event took place which turned the debate about drugs in sport upside down.
lines.zh: 但今年稍早舉辦了一場運動賽事，徹底翻轉了運動禁藥的爭論。

lines.en: Here's Asma Khalid from BBC World Service's The Global Story to explain: This weekend, elite athletes from around the world are descending on Las Vegas, Nevada, for the first-of-its-kind sporting competition known as The Enhanced Games.
lines.zh: 這是 BBC 世界廣播《The Global Story》的 Asma Khalid 的說明：這個週末，來自世界各地的頂尖運動員齊聚內華達州拉斯維加斯，參加首創的運動競賽「增強運動會」（The Enhanced Games）。

lines.en: It's kind of like the Olympics, but only for swimming, sprinting and weightlifting.
lines.zh: 它有點像奧運，但只有游泳、短跑和舉重。

lines.en: The aim is to break world records.
lines.zh: 目標是打破世界紀錄。

lines.en: In fact, some of these competitors are former Olympians – medallists battling it out for money and glory.
lines.zh: 事實上，有些參賽者是前奧運選手——這些獎牌得主為了獎金和榮耀一決高下。

lines.en: But there's one big difference...
lines.zh: 但有一個很大的不同……

lines.en: The big difference is that The Enhanced Games allow athletes to use performance-enhancing drugs that are banned in professional sports.
lines.zh: 最大的不同是，增強運動會允許運動員使用職業運動中禁止的提升表現藥物。

lines.en: In these games, nicknamed The Doping Olympics, steroids, growth hormones and stimulants are all OK.
lines.zh: 在這個被戲稱為「禁藥奧運」的運動會上，類固醇、生長激素和興奮劑全都沒問題。

lines.en: You're a big sports fan, Neil.
lines.zh: Neil，你是個大運動迷。

lines.en: Would you enjoy watching a sport where the athletes have taken drugs?
lines.zh: 你會喜歡看運動員用過藥的比賽嗎？

lines.en: No, I wouldn't.
lines.zh: 不，我不會。

lines.en: I really don't think that's fair.
lines.zh: 我真的覺得那樣不公平。

lines.en: I think we need to know that all the athletes start and compete from the same level.
lines.zh: 我覺得我們需要知道所有運動員都是從同樣的水準起步、在同樣的水準上競爭。

lines.en: Yeah, I guess that makes sense.
lines.zh: 嗯，我想這很合理。

lines.en: I don't really watch that many sports so I guess I wouldn't notice the difference, but if you're really into sport you care about the rules, right?
lines.zh: 我其實不太看運動比賽，所以我應該看不出差別，但如果你真的很熱衷運動，就會在乎規則，對吧？

lines.en: Yes, absolutely.
lines.zh: 對，絕對是。

lines.en: And in this episode we'll dive into the controversial world of The Enhanced Games, learning some useful new words and phrases along the way.
lines.zh: 在這一集，我們會深入探討增強運動會這個充滿爭議的世界，並一路學些實用的新單字和片語。

lines.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary, plus a quiz and a worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 別忘了，所有詞彙以及測驗和學習單，都可以在我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 找到。

lines.en: But now I have a question for you, Neil.
lines.zh: 不過現在，Neil，我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: You mentioned the famous sporting cheat Lance Armstrong, but how many times did Lance Armstrong win the famous race, the Tour de France, before he was finally caught out?
lines.zh: 你提到了知名的運動作弊者 Lance Armstrong，那麼他在最後被抓到之前，贏過知名的環法自行車賽幾次？

lines.en: Was it: a) five, b) six, or c) seven?
lines.zh: 是：a) 五次、b) 六次，還是 c) 七次？

lines.en: Ooh... Well, it was a lot, so I think I'll go for c) seven.
lines.zh: 喔……嗯，很多次，所以我想我選 c) 七次。

lines.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
lines.zh: 我們會在節目最後揭曉答案。

lines.en: Now, it's no exaggeration to say that The Enhanced Games are controversial.
lines.zh: 說增強運動會充滿爭議，一點也不誇張。

lines.en: After all, organisations like the World Anti-Doping Agency have spent decades fighting performance-enhancing drugs in sport.
lines.zh: 畢竟，像世界反禁藥組織這樣的機構，已經花了數十年對抗運動中的提升表現藥物。

lines.en: Here's BBC sports editor Dan Roan on World Service programme The Global Story.
lines.zh: 這是 BBC 體育編輯 Dan Roan 在世界廣播節目《The Global Story》中的說法。

lines.en: I think it's fair to say it's one of the most divisive and controversial events that the world of sport has seen for a long time.
lines.zh: 我想可以說，這是體育界很久以來最具分歧、最具爭議的賽事之一。

lines.en: It's an event where performance-enhancing drugs, banned elsewhere in mainstream sport of course, are actually allowed to be taken by the competitors under medical supervision.
lines.zh: 在這個賽事中，提升表現的藥物——當然，在其他主流運動中是禁止的——實際上允許參賽者在醫療監督下使用。

lines.en: Dan Roan says, It's fair to say The Enhanced Games are controversial.
lines.zh: Dan Roan 說：It's fair to say（可以說）增強運動會充滿爭議。

lines.en: He uses the phrase 'it's fair to say' to introduce a statement that he considers to be balanced and reasonable – that the games are controversial.
lines.zh: 他用「it's fair to say」這個片語來帶出一個他認為持平、合理的說法——這個運動會很有爭議。

lines.en: Dan also describes the games as divisive – an adjective that means causing a lot of disagreement between people.
lines.zh: Dan 也形容這個運動會 divisive——這個形容詞的意思是在人與人之間造成很多分歧。

lines.en: Much of this disagreement is about the use of performance-enhancing drugs themselves.
lines.zh: 這些分歧大多是關於使用提升表現藥物本身。

lines.en: The Games' organisers point out that all drugs are approved by the US Food and Drug Agency and taken openly under medical supervision, which they say makes them safer than when they are taken secretly at competitions elsewhere.
lines.zh: 運動會的主辦單位指出，所有藥物都經過美國食品藥物管理局核准，並在醫療監督下公開使用，他們說這比在其他比賽中偷偷用藥更安全。

lines.en: But there are many critics too, as Dan Roan outlined to BBC World Service's The Global Story.
lines.zh: 但也有很多批評者，就像 Dan Roan 向 BBC 世界廣播《The Global Story》概述的。

lines.en: But the critics, of course, say that this crosses an ethical line, that it sets a dreadful example because it risks normalising doping.
lines.zh: 但批評者當然會說，這越過了道德界線，樹立了一個很糟的榜樣，因為它有讓用禁藥變得正常化的風險。

lines.en: It could harm the integrity, therefore, of sport, and it could be dangerous to the health of those taking part.
lines.zh: 因此，它可能會損害運動的誠信，也可能危害參賽者的健康。

lines.en: For the Games' critics, doping crosses an ethical line.
lines.zh: 對運動會的批評者來說，用禁藥越過了道德界線。

lines.en: The phrase 'to cross the line' means to start behaving in a way that's not socially acceptable.
lines.zh: 片語「to cross the line」的意思是開始做出社會無法接受的行為。

lines.en: These critics say the Games set a bad example, meaning that they encourage others to behave badly as well.
lines.zh: 這些批評者說這個運動會 set a bad example，意思是它會鼓勵其他人也做出不好的行為。

lines.en: Why is that, Pippa?
lines.zh: 為什麼呢，Pippa？

lines.en: Well, it's because critics argue the games normalise the use of performance drugs in sport.
lines.zh: 嗯，因為批評者認為這個運動會讓運動中使用提升表現藥物變得正常化。

lines.en: If you normalise something, you treat it as normal or acceptable when previously it wasn't.
lines.zh: 如果你 normalise 某件事，就是把以前不被接受的事當成正常或可以接受的。

lines.en: But with arguments strongly held on both sides, the debate is far from over.
lines.zh: 但雙方都有強烈的論點，這場爭論還遠遠沒有結束。

lines.en: So Neil, have you changed your opinion after hearing both sides of the story?
lines.zh: Neil，聽了雙方的說法後，你有改變看法嗎？

lines.en: No, I haven't.
lines.zh: 不，沒有。

lines.en: I think it's just not fair, and I think if you're not fair in sport, what's the point?
lines.zh: 我覺得這就是不公平，而且如果運動不公平，那還有什麼意義？

lines.en: Well, let's hear the answer to my quiz question, Neil.
lines.zh: 好，Neil，我們來聽我的問題答案。

lines.en: I asked you how many times Lance Armstrong won the Tour de France, and it was c) seven times, consecutively between 1999 and 2005.
lines.zh: 我問你 Lance Armstrong 贏過環法自行車賽幾次，答案是 c) 七次，1999 年到 2005 年連續奪冠。

lines.en: Of course, we now know that there were performance-enhancing drugs involved.
lines.zh: 當然，我們現在知道那背後有提升表現的藥物。

lines.en: OK. So, now it's time to recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with 'doping' – using banned drugs to perform better in sporting competitions.
lines.zh: 好。現在來複習今天學到的詞彙，首先是「doping」——在運動比賽中使用禁藥以提升表現。

lines.en: You can use the phrase 'it's fair to say' to introduce a statement you consider to be balanced, reasonable or true.
lines.zh: 你可以用「it's fair to say」這個片語，來帶出一個你認為持平、合理或正確的說法。

lines.en: If something is divisive, it causes disagreement between people.
lines.zh: 如果某件事是 divisive，就是它會在人與人之間造成分歧。

lines.en: The idiom 'cross the line' means to start behaving in an unacceptable way.
lines.zh: 慣用語「cross the line」的意思是開始做出不可接受的行為。

lines.en: If you set a bad example, you behave in a way that encourages others to behave badly.
lines.zh: 如果你 set a bad example，就是你的行為會鼓勵別人也做出不好的行為。

lines.en: And finally, 'to normalise something' means to treat it as normal or acceptable when previously it wasn't.
lines.zh: 最後，「to normalise something」的意思是把以前不被接受的事當成正常或可接受的。

lines.en: OK. Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to practise more, you'll find a quiz and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 好。我們的六分鐘又到了，不過如果你想多練習，我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 上有測驗和學習單。

lines.en: See you again soon.
lines.zh: 很快再見。

lines.en: But for now it's goodbye.
lines.zh: 但現在要說再見了。

lines.en: Bye!
lines.zh: 拜拜！
